1	# Repository Parallelizer
     2	
     3	Manage multiple related git repositories as a single project — with parallel workspaces, branch orchestration, and a web-based GUI.
     4	
     5	## What Is This?
     6	
     7	When a project spans several git repositories, keeping them in sync is tedious: cloning each one, switching branches across all of them, remembering which repos belong together. **Repository Parallelizer** treats a group of repos as one "project" and lets you create isolated **workspaces** — each with its own branch configuration, cloned copies, and a ready-to-open VS Code `.code-workspace` file.
     8	
     9	Set up a project once, then spin up as many parallel workspaces as you need — one for the main branch, one for a feature, one for a hotfix — without stepping on your own toes.
    10	
    11	## Features
    12	
    13	- **Project-based repo grouping** — register repositories once, then combine them into projects.
    14	- **Parallel workspaces** — create multiple independent workspaces per project, each with its own branch assignments and cloned copies.
    15	- **One-click branch switching** — switch branches across all repos in a workspace in a single operation, with conflict detection.
    16	- **VS Code integration** — auto-generated `.code-workspace` files let you open an entire workspace in VS Code instantly.
    17	- **Web GUI** — a built-in browser UI for managing repositories, projects, workspaces, and branches — no terminal required after setup. The project dashboard supports real-time filtering by name/ID/description, repository filtering, and sort by alphabetical or last-activity order.
    18	- **Live git status** — automatic polling shows current branches, uncommitted changes, and unfetched commits at a glance.
    19	- **Workspace health checks** — detect and fix configuration drift (missing repos, stale workspace files, credential errors).
    20	- **Interactive CLI** — a keyboard-driven terminal menu for quick access to setup, server launch, and documentation generation.
    21	- **Private repo support** — per-host credential management for cloning private repositories.
    22	
    23	## How Does This Compare to Git Worktrees?
    24	
    25	Git worktrees let you check out multiple branches of a **single** repository side by side — great when your entire project lives in one repo. Repository Parallelizer solves a different problem: when your project spans **multiple** repositories that need to move together.
    26	
    27	| | Git Worktrees | Repository Parallelizer |
    28	|---|---|---|
    29	| **Scope** | One repository, multiple branches | Multiple repositories, multiple branches |
    30	| **Branch switching** | Per-repo only | Coordinated across all repos at once |
    31	| **VS Code workspace** | Manual setup | Auto-generated `.code-workspace` files |
    32	| **Status overview** | Per-repo (`git status`) | Aggregated across all repos in a workspace |
    33	
    34	If your project is a single repo, worktrees are the simpler choice. If you're juggling a frontend, backend, shared library, and infrastructure repo that all need to be on the same feature branch — that's where this tool comes in.
    35	
    36	## Requirements
    37	
    38	- **Node.js** >= 18
    39	- **npm** >= 9
    40	- **git** >= 2.28
    41	
    42	## Quick Start
    43	
    44	```bash
    45	# Clone and build
    46	git clone https://github.com/Mistralys/repo-parallelizer.git
    47	cd repo-parallelizer
    48	npm install
    49	npm run build
    50	
    51	# Run the setup wizard to create your config
    52	npm link
    53	paralizer setup
    54	
    55	# Launch the GUI
    56	paralizer serve
    57	```
    58	
    59	The setup wizard walks you through creating a `config.json` with your projects folder and storage location. Once complete, open `http://localhost:4200` in your browser to start managing your repositories.
    60	
    61	### Alternative: run without installing globally
    62	
    63	```bash
    64	# Unix / macOS
    65	./menu.sh
    66	
    67	# Windows
    68	menu.cmd
    69	```
    70	
    71	### CLI commands
    72	
    73	| Command | Description |
    74	|---------|-------------|
    75	| `paralizer` | Open the interactive CLI menu |
    76	| `paralizer serve` | Start the GUI server directly |
    77	| `paralizer setup` | Run the setup wizard |
    78	| `paralizer docs` | Generate project documentation |
    79	
    80	## Start with Windows
    81	
    82	1. Press `Win + R`, type the following command to open your user Startup folder, and press **Enter**:
    83	   ```
    84	   shell:startup
    85	   ```
    86	   *(This opens the folder: `C:\Users\<YourUsername>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup`)*
    87	
    88	2. In that folder, right-click an empty area and select **New** > **Text Document**.
    89	3. Name it `start-repo-parallelizer.vbs` (ensure you delete the `.txt` extension!).
    90	4. Right-click the new file, select **Edit** (or open it with Notepad/VS Code), and paste the following code into it:
    91	
    92	   ```vbscript
    93	   Set WshShell = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
    94	   ' 0 means the window will be hidden, so you don't have a lingering terminal
    95	   WshShell.Run "cmd /c paralizer serve", 0
    96	   Set WshShell = Nothing
    97	   ```
    98	
    99	   > **Requires `npm link`** — run `npm link` once in the project folder so `paralizer` is available globally.

1	# Constraints & Conventions
     2	
     3	## TypeScript Import Extensions
     4	
     5	All relative imports **must** include the `.js` extension:
     6	
     7	```typescript
     8	// Correct
     9	import { MyClass } from './my-module.js';
    10	
    11	// Wrong — compile error + runtime failure
    12	import { MyClass } from './my-module';
    13	```
    14	
    15	This is a strict requirement of the `Node16` module resolution setting. TypeScript maps `.js` → `.ts` at compile time and emits `.js` unchanged for Node.js at runtime.
    16	
    17	## Git Subprocess Security
    18	
    19	- All Git commands use `shell: false` — no shell expansion, globbing, or metacharacter processing.
    20	- Arguments are passed as a typed `string[]` directly to `spawn()`.
    21	- Error messages use only `args[0]` (the subcommand name), never the full args array, to avoid leaking credential-bearing URLs.
    22	- `RepositoryManager.add()` redacts embedded credentials from URLs before interpolating into error messages.
    23	- `runGit()` always sets `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` and `GIT_ASKPASS=echo` on every spawned subprocess. This prevents interactive credential prompts and credential-helper (osxkeychain, libsecret) blocking on unauthenticated requests. Do not remove either env var.
    24	- **Standing rule — credential stripping in git error output:** When credential injection is wired into future WPs (i.e., `injectCredentialToken()` is used to append tokens to URLs before passing to `runGit()`/`runGitOrThrow()`), all code paths that surface `GitResult.stderr` in thrown Error messages, log output, or API responses **must** apply `stripEmbeddedCredentials()` (from `src/git/git-credentials.ts`) to the stderr string first. Git may echo the credentialed URL back in error messages (e.g., `fatal: repository https://ghp_token@github.com/... not found`), which would expose the PAT. This is a non-optional security control for every credential-injection WP.
    25	- **Credential injection lifetime contract:** `injectCredentialToken()` must only be called immediately before a git subprocess invocation — never stored or returned through API boundaries. The injected URL must not appear in log output, API responses, or Error messages without first passing through `stripEmbeddedCredentials()`.
    26	- **Pre-embedded-credentials passthrough:** If a repo URL already contains embedded credentials (detected via `hasEmbeddedCredentials()`) orchestrator implementations **must** call `hasEmbeddedCredentials()` before invoking `resolveCredential()` + `injectCredentialToken()` and decide explicitly whether to strip and re-inject or reject the URL.- **Token masking rule (API responses):** The `gitCredentials` field in `AppConfig` / `config.json` stores **plaintext** tokens. No API handler, logger, or error message may expose a plaintext token in any response. All credential API responses must pass the array through `buildMaskedCredentials()` (in `src/server/routes/config.ts`) before serialisation — this applies `maskToken()` to every `token` field in each `GitCredentialEntry`, producing `****` + last-4-chars (e.g. `****abc1`). Tokens shorter than 4 characters are fully masked as `****`. This is a non-optional security control: any new credential endpoint **must** apply `buildMaskedCredentials()` before calling `sendJson()`.
    27	## Credential Field Validation
    28	
    29	### Hostname Format (`host` field)
    30	
    31	The `host` field in a `GitCredentialEntry` must not contain `/`, `\`, null bytes (`\0`), or whitespace characters. These characters are invalid in a hostname and are rejected with HTTP 400 by `PUT /api/config/credentials`. The validation regex is `/[/\\\0\s]/`. Valid examples: `github.com`, `gitlab.example.com`.
    32	
    33	### Per-Field Length Limits
    34	
    35	| Field | Maximum length |
    36	|---|---|
    37	| `id` | 100 characters |
    38	| `label` | 200 characters |
    39	| `host` | 253 characters |
    40	| `token` | 500 characters |
    41	
    42	These limits are enforced both at the API boundary (`PUT /api/config/credentials` → HTTP 400 on violation) and during config file parsing (`parseGitCredentials()` → `Error` thrown on violation). Values exactly at each limit are accepted.
    43	
    44	**API whitespace normalization:** `PUT /api/config/credentials` trims leading and trailing whitespace from `id`, `label`, and `token` before storage. This is intentional UX normalization (e.g., clipboard pastes with trailing newlines). The stored value may therefore differ from what was submitted. The `host` field is handled differently: whitespace is rejected outright (HTTP 400) rather than stripped, because whitespace is structurally invalid in a hostname.
    45	
    46	**Config parser non-normalization:** `parseGitCredentials()` applies `.trim()` only to *measure* field length during validation — it does not normalize the values it returns. The in-memory `GitCredentialEntry[]` array reflects the raw strings from `config.json`, including any surrounding whitespace. Code that consumes parsed credentials should trim field values before use if the config.json source is untrusted or manually edited. The API route handler, by contrast, always produces and stores clean (trimmed) values.
    47	
    48	### Host/Credential Coherence (`PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential`)
    49	
    50	When assigning a credential to a repository, the API validates that `credential.host` matches the hostname extracted from the repository's URL via `extractHost()`. If they do not match, the request is rejected with HTTP 400 and a descriptive error message indicating both the credential's host and the repository URL's host. This guard prevents silent credential misrouting. The check is skipped when:
    51	- `credentialId` is `null` (clearing the association is always allowed).
    52	- The repository URL is not an HTTPS URL (SSH URLs return `null` from `extractHost()`).
    53	
    54	## Stateless Managers
    55	
    56	All model managers (`RepositoryManager`, `ProjectManager`, `WorkspaceManager`) re-read their backing JSON file from disk on **every** public method call. There is no in-memory cache. This ensures concurrent writes from other processes are always reflected.
    57	
    58	## ID Validation Rules
    59	
    60	| Entity | Format | Validation Function |
    61	|---|---|---|
    62	| Repository ID | Lowercase kebab-case (`a-z0-9`, segments separated by `-`) | `isValidKebabCase()` |
    63	| Project ID | Lowercase kebab-case | `isValidKebabCase()` |
    64	| Workspace ID | 2–10 uppercase ASCII letters (`A-Z`) | `isValidWorkspaceId()` |
    65	
    66	Path-traversal sequences, uppercase characters (for kebab-case IDs), spaces, and other invalid formats are rejected with a descriptive error.
    67	
    68	## The STABLE Workspace Invariant
    69	
    70	Every project has exactly one workspace with ID `"STABLE"`. It is auto-created when a project is created and **cannot be removed or renamed**. The STABLE workspace is intended for the remote's default branch.
    71	
    72	## Path Resolution
    73	
    74	Both `storageFolder` and `projectsFolder` in `config.json` accept relative or absolute paths:
    75	
    76	- **Relative paths** are resolved against the tool root (directory containing `package.json`), regardless of the current working directory when the tool is invoked.
    77	- **Absolute paths** are used as-is.
    78	
    79	## Configuration
    80	
    81	- `config.json` is created by copying `config.dist.json`. It is not committed (gitignored).
    82	- The `_instructions` key in `config.dist.json` is an editorial note and is not a valid config field. Remove it from `config.json`.
    83	- `initializeStorage()` is idempotent — re-running it does not overwrite existing files.
    84	- **`DEFAULTS` Pick maintenance:** The exported `DEFAULTS` constant in `src/config/config.ts` is typed as `Pick<AppConfig, 'cloneDepth' | 'serverPort' | 'gitPollingIntervalSeconds' | 'notesCardHeight' | 'notesColumns'>`. When a new non-optional, non-required `AppConfig` field with a sensible default is added, **three** coordinated changes are required: (1) add the field key to the `Pick` union, (2) add the field's default value to the `DEFAULTS` object literal, and (3) add the fallback guard in `loadConfig()` (e.g. `typeof raw['field'] === 'number' ? raw['field'] : DEFAULTS.field`). Omitting step (1) is a TypeScript compile error; omitting steps (2)–(3) causes the field to be `undefined` at runtime for configs that predate the new field.
    85	- **`_defaultsCoverageGuard` pattern:** Immediately after `DEFAULTS`, a `const _defaultsCoverageGuard: AppConfig = { ...DEFAULTS, projectsFolder: '', storageFolder: '' } satisfies AppConfig` expression is declared and voided. The `satisfies AppConfig` clause is a compile-time completeness guard: if a new required field is added to `AppConfig` without a corresponding entry in `DEFAULTS` or the guard literal, TypeScript emits a type error at that exact line. Do not remove this guard — it is the automated enforcement mechanism for the DEFAULTS maintenance rule above.
    86	
    87	## Schema Version Policy
    88	
    89	The `SchemaVersion` field on `BaseStore` tracks structural changes to persisted JSON store files. The rule is defined in `src/storage/storage.types.ts`:
    90	
    91	- **Do NOT bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`** when adding an **optional** field. Existing JSON files that lack the field are still valid — no migration is required.
    92	- **Do bump `SCHEMA_VERSION`** (and add a migration step) for breaking changes: removing a required field, renaming a field, or changing the type of an existing field in a way that would cause older JSON files to fail validation or produce incorrect behaviour.
    93	
    94	**Example:** `Repository.CredentialId` is an optional field addition — existing `repositories.json` files remain valid without it. No `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump was needed for this change.
    95	
    96	## Test Conventions
    97	
    98	- **Test runner:** Node.js built-in test runner (`node --test`).
    99	- **Cleanup:** All tests creating temporary files must register a `process.on('exit')` handler for synchronous cleanup, in addition to `afterAll`. The `'exit'` event fires on `SIGINT` or crash.
   100	- **Network tests:** Tests requiring outbound internet set `SKIP_NETWORK_TESTS=1` to self-skip.

101	- **Fake-git binary pattern:** To test CLI argument construction (e.g., verifying credential-injected URLs are passed correctly to `cloneRepository()`), use a fake git binary stub rather than module mocking or network calls. The stub is a shell script placed in a uniquely-prefixed temp directory that is prepended to `process.env.PATH` for the test duration; it writes all received arguments to a capture file and exits with a non-zero code. The original PATH is always restored in a `finally` block. This approach is necessary because modern git (2.x/libcurl) strips embedded credentials from its own error messages, making the injected-URL string unavailable in `stderr`. The shared implementation lives in `src/tests/test-helpers.ts` (`setupFakeGit()`). **Note:** PATH mutation is not concurrency-safe — this pattern is safe only because the test runner executes test files sequentially.
   102	
   103	## GUI Frontend Conventions
   104	
   105	- **Router injection:** Views needing programmatic navigation export `setRouter(router)` and receive the router via dependency injection from `app.js`. Direct imports of `router.js` from views are forbidden (circular dependency).
   106	- **Cleanup contract:** Views with side-effects (intervals, event listeners) must return a cleanup function from their render entry point. The router calls it before rendering the next view.
   107	- **No framework:** Vanilla JavaScript with ES modules. No build step for the frontend.
   108	- **JSON key normalisation:** The backend uses PascalCase keys (`Id`, `Name`, `Url`). The `normalise.js` utility maps them to camelCase for frontend use.
   109	
   110	## Vendor CSS Assets
   111	
   112	The `gui/public/css/vendor/` directory contains CSS files copied from `node_modules` by the `copy-vendor` npm script. These are **generated artifacts** and must not be committed to version control (gitignored). After cloning the repo, run `npm install` — the `postinstall` hook will automatically populate the vendor directory. Currently contains `pico.classless.min.css` from `@picocss/pico`.
   113	
   114	## Build Output
   115	
   116	- Compiled output goes to `dist/`. Source maps are generated alongside each `.js` file.
   117	- `dist/` is excluded from version control.
   118	- `dist/index.js` does not carry the executable bit after `tsc`. Use `npm link` or `node dist/index.js`.
   119	
   120	## Request Body Limit
   121	
   122	`parseJsonBody()` enforces a **1 MB** request body size limit.
   123	
   124	## Timeout Constants
   125	
   126	| Constant | Value | Used By |
   127	|---|---|---|
   128	| `CLONE_TIMEOUT_MS` | 120,000 ms (2 min) | `cloneRepository()` via orchestrators |
   129	| `FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS` | 30,000 ms (30 sec) | `fetchRemote()` via polling and branch operations |
   130	
   131	## Config Validation Constants
   132	
   133	All validation bounds for `AppConfig` fields are defined in `src/config/config.constants.ts` and imported by route handlers. Route-level validation enforces integer-only values within these ranges; `loadConfig()` applies defaults but does not clamp out-of-range values.
   134	
   135	| Constant | Value | Field | Description |
   136	|---|---|---|---|
   137	| `MIN_POLLING_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | 10 | `gitPollingIntervalSeconds` | Minimum polling interval (seconds) |
   138	| `MAX_POLLING_INTERVAL_SECONDS` | 86,400 | `gitPollingIntervalSeconds` | Maximum polling interval (24 hours) |
   139	| `MIN_NOTES_CARD_HEIGHT` | 120 | `notesCardHeight` | Minimum note card height (px) |
   140	| `MAX_NOTES_CARD_HEIGHT` | 800 | `notesCardHeight` | Maximum note card height (px) |
   141	| `DEFAULT_NOTES_CARD_HEIGHT` | 220 | `notesCardHeight` | Default note card height (px) |
   142	| `MIN_NOTES_COLUMNS` | 1 | `notesColumns` | Minimum column count in the notes view grid |
   143	| `MAX_NOTES_COLUMNS` | 6 | `notesColumns` | Maximum column count in the notes view grid |
   144	| `DEFAULT_NOTES_COLUMNS` | 2 | `notesColumns` | Default column count in the notes view grid |
   145	
   146	## Type-Audit Acceptance Criterion
   147	
   148	Any work package that adds or modifies exported types must include the following acceptance criterion:
   149	
   150	> **Type audit:** Exported types match the plan specification — verify that each new/modified interface property name, type, and optionality align with the plan before marking the WP complete.
   151	
   152	QA work packages that follow implementation WPs should cross-check type signatures against the plan, paying particular attention to optional (`?`) vs. required properties and union types.
   153	
   154	## Known Input Validation Gaps
   155	
   156	- `branchExists()` and `fetchRemote()` do not validate the `'-'` prefix guard that `createBranch()` and `switchBranch()` enforce. These are lower-risk (no data-loss path) and a guard is planned for a future cleanup.
   157	- `branchName` in `branchExists()` is not validated against a safe refname pattern — a path-traversal value may yield a false-positive. Callers must validate before passing untrusted input.
